q1: SELECT beer.name, min_price, bar FROM beer LEFT OUTER JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS min_price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS t ON beer.name = t.beer LEFT OUTER JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer AND min_price = serves.price
q2: SELECT beer.name AS beer, min_price.price AS price, serves.bar AS bar FROM beer LEFT JOIN serves ON beer.name = serves.beer LEFT JOIN (SELECT beer, MIN(price) AS price FROM serves GROUP BY beer) AS min_price ON serves.beer = min_price.beer AND serves.price = min_price.price ORDER BY beer.name

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because of the order of JOIN operations and the placement of conditions in the WHERE clause. Q1 first performs the JOINs and then applies the conditions, while Q2 applies the conditions during the JOINs. This can lead to different results if the conditions are not commutative.
